script.title: How a Pile of Rubble Taught Us to Read Hieroglyphs
script.hook_text: Soldiers found it in a wall
sentences: French soldiers rebuilding a fort wall accidentally unlocked ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs.
In July 1799, French troops were repairing Fort Julien near Rosetta, Egypt.
Lieutenant Pierre-François Bouchard noticed a carved slab used as building material.
The stone contained three distinct scripts, but no one alive could read the top lines.
The bottom text was Ancient Greek, which scholars already understood.
Since all three scripts held versions of the same decree, the Greek text unlocked the symbols.
That salvaged wall stone became the Rosetta Stone, now the British Museum's most visited object.
script.description:
How a piece of building rubble in a French fort became the key to understanding ancient Egypt.
Soldiers found the stone in 1799, changing history forever.
claims_en: French soldiers found the Rosetta Stone in July 1799.
The stone was found during repairs to Fort Julien near Rosetta, Egypt.
Lieutenant Pierre-François Bouchard identified the stone's potential importance.
The stone contains three scripts: Hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Ancient Greek.
It contains a decree issued in 196 BC.
Because the three scripts represent versions of the same text, the Greek version was used to decipher the Egyptian scripts.
The Rosetta Stone is the most visited object in the British Museum.
